webster.text: A speech or discourse composed according to the rules of oratory, and spoken in public.

more.text: In modern usage, an oration differs from a sermon, from an argument at the bar, and from a speech before a deliberative assembly.
A harangue; a public speech or address.

example.quote: Such improper confidence Demosthenes was so well convinced had ruined his country, that in his second Philippic oration he remarks “that there is one common bulwark with which men of prudence are naturally provided, the guard and security of all people, particularly of free states, against the assaults of tyrants What is this?
example.cite: Cato, Letter VII, New York Journal
